items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I also wanted to play with some of the jazz musicians that I’d admired on records and heard about, and was able to do. Among them, the first that come to mind are Buddy Collette and Bud Shank, Conte Candoli, Shelly Manne, Red Mitchell.

ctx.x: I bet. Speaking of wonderful moments, your move up to Los Angeles, can you recall the feeling of perhaps nervousness, anticipation the first time you did a significant studio date?

Well okay, the first recording studio date I did, back in those days there were a lot of TV shows that had live bands: Sonny & Cher, Glen Campbell, Carol Burnett come to mind. They had rehearsal pianists and those were guys that worked with the choreographer and bandleader in mapping out medleys. And I was working on the Oral Roberts TV show. He was a Christian faith healer who also had a university in Oklahoma, I’m sure most people know of him. And he had this television show with a choreographer. I was the…
It must have been a big decision to move – you know across the country to New York after you’ve established yourself in Los Angeles. What was the impetus for that?
